question: Does the now-accessible Matillano 2011 thesis support public freshwater species occurrences for Lake Manguao and northern Palawan rivers?

accessUpdate.priorStatus: An earlier review had only the official record, abstract and indexed excerpts because the cached signed PDF URL returned 403.
accessUpdate.currentStatus: The current SUNY ESF portal record exposes the full 67-page thesis PDF. The title/copyright page and study methods, material examined, selected tables, discussion and specimen-deposition statement were reviewed.

studyScope.discipline: Morphological taxonomy and conservation assessment of Puntius populations, not a comprehensive Palawan fish inventory.
studyScope.geographicScope: Study-area prose names Lake Manguao, Ibangley River, Langogan River, Babuyan River and Iwahig River; the figure also labels Maoyon River, a Babuyan tributary. Material-examined text names Lake Manguao, Manguao Stream, Langogan, Balsahan (Iwahig tributary), Babuyan and Maoyon samples.
studyScope.methods: The thesis says lake and river collection sites were GPS-located with a handheld Garmin eTrex and sampled Puntius with beach seine, hook and line, push net and gill nets. Specimens were photographed, tagged with JDM alphanumeric codes and preserved for morphological/meristic study.
habitats: Lake Manguao open-water and littoral zones
Manguao Stream, a tributary flowing into Lake Manguao
Named riverine Puntius populations in northern Palawan

lakeUnresolvedMorphotypes: Puntius sp. 1, described from Lake Manguao open water
Puntius sp. 2, described from Manguao Stream, a lake tributary
evidenceFindings.riverTaxonLabels: Populations from Langogan, Balsahan/Iwahig, Babuyan and Maoyon are labeled Puntius cf. binotatus in the thesis. The cf. qualifier means the field identification is tentative and must not be normalized to an unqualified species occurrence without a new independent identification.
evidenceFindings.siteEvidence: The full text gives named collection-site descriptions and GPS coordinates for selected sampled populations. This review does not reproduce the coordinates or specimen list because the thesis is all-rights-reserved and the site/specimen records have not been independently reconciled.
evidenceFindings.historicalTaxonomy: The thesis's Lake Manguao names are historical source usages. The previously reviewed current Catalog of Fishes crosswalk treats the bantolanensis name as a synonym of valid Barbodes manguaoensis. That nomenclatural result does not re-identify the thesis specimens, settle the thesis's biological interpretation, or match either unresolved morphotype.

integrityFindings.specimenCount: The material-examined section states 80 specimens. The named groups and counts displayed in that roster total 70; Table 2 shows an Ibangley River population not enumerated in the material-examined list. The missing ten-specimen roster entry is unresolved and is not inferred.
integrityFindings.specimenCodeIssues: One Balsahan specimen code, JDM-0448, is printed twice; one Langogan item is marked No tag. No official accession crosswalk is provided.
integrityFindings.specimenCustody: The thesis says examined specimens remained in the author's collection pending further study and that final repositories were still to be determined among the Philippine National Museum, Western Philippines University and museums in the United States.
integrityFindings.dates: No field collection dates appear in the reviewed material-examined roster. The 2011 thesis year is not used as a specimen collection date.
integrityFindings.taxonomyScope: The thesis concerns one minnow genus. Two lake morphotypes remain unnamed; river populations are identified only as cf. binotatus. It cannot serve as a complete Lake Manguao or Palawan freshwater checklist.
integrityFindings.license: The thesis title/copyright page states © 2011 J. D. Matillano, all rights reserved. The SUNY ESF portal's open-access label enables access to read/download the document but is not a reuse license. No text, table, figure, specimen code or coordinate data is republished here.

followUp.nextAction: Use the thesis to identify candidate lake/river sites for a separate query of openly reusable occurrence records and current taxonomic resources. Hold all thesis-derived names, specimen data and coordinates from public app rows pending roster reconciliation, specimen-voucher crosswalk and explicit reuse permission. Continue other Palawan freshwater and estuary sources independently.

sources.supports: Official SUNY ESF record, bibliographic metadata, abstract, thesis access label and link to the full text.
Previously reviewed current Catalog of Fishes synonymy for historical Barbus/Puntius bantolanensis and Barbodes manguaoensis; taxonomic name crosswalk only.
